title: QBR - Venturi Platform Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check covering usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, security questions, and alignment on roadmap. Customer is generally satisfied with performance but flagged increased token costs and two recent timeouts on large-batch inference. Action items: Redwood to share detailed cost breakdown, run targeted benchmark on their 8k context model on Dedicated, and provide SOC2 + KMS docs. Next meeting to review POC results by end of month.
topics: recent reliability incidents (timeouts on batch jobs)
roadmap alignment and upcoming features (batching improvements, quantization profiles)
next steps: benchmark, pricing, security pack
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-10 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE); Elena Gomez (Venturi), Samir Khan (Venturi), Aisha Roberts (Venturi Sec), Jon Li (Venturi SRE)

0:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, appreciate you carving out time. Quick agenda: usage/costs, reliability incidents, security check, then roadmap and next steps.
0:18 - Elena: thanks Maya. Quick callout, overall things are good, latency's been solid for our 2k flows, but we saw a couple issues last month when we moved to larger batch runs for nightly indexing.
0:32 - Diego: yep, saw the logs you pasted, looks like two timeout events on 2026-02-22 around 02:13 UTC, likely due to the large 8k sequence runs plus concurrent spikes.
0:45 - Samir: curious then on cost - tokens and compute spiked too, our bill shot up 28% month-over-month and we need to justify it to finance.
1:02 - Ravi: understood. We pulled a cost breakdown; most of the increase is model context length and replays for failed batches. We'll share the per-route token heatmap after this call.
1:20 - Aisha: on security, we need to make sure Private deployment is still on the table for data residency. Also we need KMS integration details for key rotation.
1:38 - Maya: absolutely, we'll send SOC 2 attestations and the KMS integration guide. For Private, the typical path is a Dedicated trial first, or full Private (VPC) depending on your timeline.
1:55 - Jon: can you remind us about autoscaling behavior for Dedicated fleets? We saw some lag when spike happened.
2:12 - Diego: auto-scale has a cold-start window and burst policies. For your workload (mixed latency-sensitive small requests and nightly long-batch jobs) we usually recommend a dedicated pool with burst capacity plus pre-warmed instances for the nightly window. We can set the policy to pre-warm N instances at 01:30 UTC.
2:34 - Elena: that would help. Also, any quick wins on cost? We tried the cache TTL but it didn't move the needle much.
2:48 - Diego: quick wins: prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, quantization on non-critical models (we have 4-bit profiles), and smarter batching rules to avoid retries. We'll propose a config you can apply.
3:05 - Samir: can you run a benchmark of our 8k context model on Dedicated? We want an apples-to-apples on latency and throughput for our peak windows.
3:20 - Maya: yes, Diego can run that with your sample prompts. We'll need a small test dataset and preferred SLA target.
3:33 - Aisha: security pack please — SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML config, RBAC, audit logs retention, and our KMS questions.
3:45 - Ravi: we'll package those docs. Note: our SOC 2 report is the latest from Dec 2025. KMS flows show we support Cloud KMS and customer-managed HSM in Private.
4:02 - Jon: any notes on incidents — were the timeouts product bugs or capacity issues?
4:15 - Diego: our root cause points to a combination of request shaping plus a fallback that retried some requests, causing queue amplification. We fixed a retry threshold and added backpressure support in the runtime; the patch rolled out on 2026-02-25.
4:33 - Elena: thanks. After the patch we still saw one slow run, might be due to concurrency fuzz.
4:45 - Diego: let's capture that run and we'll add it to the benchmark.
5:00 - Maya: roadmap items relevant to you: improved batching heuristics (rolling out Q2), quantization profiles per model, and a new observability view in Console for per-route token and latency attribution.
5:18 - Samir: the per-route view sounds useful — our finance team keeps asking for per-feature cost.
5:30 - Maya: we'll give you access to the cost breakdown + a CSV export in the interim.
5:40 - Elena: what's the timeline if we want to pilot Dedicated for a month?
5:50 - Ravi: we can spin a small Dedicated pool within 3–5 business days once the contract hit and IP whitelisting is sorted; Private/VPC longer (4–6 weeks typical).
6:05 - Aisha: do you support SCIM for SSO?
6:15 - Maya: yes, SCIM + SAML SSO. We'll include the setup guide.
6:25 - Samir: also curious if Redwood has recommendations for reducing failed replays — our app retries on client side too.
6:40 - Diego: we recommend idempotency keys and server-side short circuit for known transient errors; we'll share best-practice doc.
6:50 - Elena: okay for next steps, I'd like the benchmark and a proposed Dedicated config.
7:02 - Maya: noted. We'll also share the cost breakdown and security pack.
7:15 - Ravi: action items and owners we'll capture now.

(Conversation continues with some interrupting chatter and clarifications; timestamps skip ahead to end-of-call recap)

40:00 - Maya: recap: Redwood to share per-route cost CSV, SOC2 + KMS docs, run Dedicated benchmark on 8k model, propose Dedicated pool sizing and autoscale policy. Venturi to provide sample prompts and test dataset, and confirm preferred dates for a one-week Dedicated pilot.
40:20 - Elena: confirmed, we'll send data by 2026-03-12.
40:30 - Samir: finance wants a cost estimate by 2026-03-18 — can you deliver?
40:40 - Maya: we'll aim for the 18th.
41:00 - Aisha: security will review the pack and get back with any follow-ups within a week.
41:15 - Maya: great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with meeting notes and links.
41:30 - Diego: I'll kick off the benchmark once I have the dataset.
41:40 - Meeting ends.
